targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-836e (interval arm, supersedes V3-EXQ-836b, THIRD and final leg of the noise-scaled MECH-476 falsifier redesign): retained_fraction across window_steps [0, 150, 400, 900] = [0.712, 0.707, 0.860, 0.723] -- spread 0.153, non-monotone (peaks at n400, not growing with interval). mean_paired_delta=0.0106 vs effective_interval_margin=0.893 (noise-scaled, sd_delta=0.595) -- effect is ~84x smaller than the margin required to call retention interval-dependent. Leave-one-out: ALL 10/10 folds (dropping each seed 42-51 individually) read 'weakened' -- fully robust, matching 836d's own 10/10 result. Concur with self-route. **THIS COMPLETES THE THREE-LEG FALSIFIER**: dose (836a, weakens), novelty-tagging (836d, weakens, reversed direction), and now interval (836e, weakens) have ALL independently and robustly found retention invariant to their respective manipulated variable. The claim's OWN pre-registered `what_would_answer` text states explicitly: 'WEAKENED if retained fraction is INVARIANT to both [dose and interval] and tracks only the concurrent constraint coefficient -- there is then no consolidation process and this claim is withdrawn into MECH-459/460.' That condition is now fully satisfied by clean, well-powered, leave-one-out-robust evidence across all three arms, with biology (Krakauer 2005, Walker 2003, Moncada & Viola 2007) established as clear and the tests as fair (per the cluster autopsy's own four-layer diagnosis, unchanged). Recommend governance apply the claim's own pre-registered disposition: WITHDRAW MECH-476, folding its content into MECH-459/460 (return_scale_invariance_blocks_actor_bootstrap and transient_behavioral_prior_bootstrap respectively) as the pre-registration specifies. This is the highest-threshold demotion path (tested fairly + biology supports the mechanism + still fails, on all three independently-designed arms) and should go through the normal /governance interactive confirmation before being applied.
